reason: The hypothesis directly mirrors the findings of E2, which reports the successful implementation of SCCPs in a tungsten-based refractory HEA, achieving the exact strength (2.15 GPa) and ductility (15%) targets, along with high-temperature performance. E1 provides general background on nanoprecipitation strategies for strength-ductility synergy but notes their limited effectiveness in refractory HEAs, setting the stage for the specific advance claimed in E2. The cited evidence fully and accurately supports all key premises.
premises: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) can be implemented in a tungsten-based refractory HEA via multi-stage thermo-mechanical processing.
SCCPs structure induces coherent particle hardening from both δ-lamella and γ″ precipitates.
SCCPs structure achieves ultrahigh strength (~2 GPa) without compromising tensile ductility (~15%) at ambient temperature.
SCCPs structure retains high strength (>1 GPa) at elevated temperatures up to 800 °C.
The improvement is relative to a single-stage processed HEA baseline.
